evidence.detail: The manager is constructed for one owning RSInterface and maintains an ordered list plus id-indexed map of InterfaceLayoutEntry objects for that interface.

Its layout pass resolves each child's direct coordinates, relative-entry dependencies, saved point anchors and proportional constraints, then writes final positions back through RSInterface.b(index, childId, x, y).

When a managed child is a DropDownComponent, the manager also lays out the shared DropDownMenuPanel directly beneath it, proving this is live interface layout authority rather than a generic collection.

evidence.detail: Each entry stores one interface/widget id and resolves that id through the global RSInterface table to expose the child's width and height.
The entry carries direct x/y coordinates, optional relative-entry dependencies with offsets, optional point-anchor dependencies and an optional InterfaceRelativeLayoutConstraint.
Its mutators configure absolute coordinates, dependency ids and offsets, relative constraints and anchor offsets, then return the same entry for chained interface construction.

evidence.detail: The value object stores a referenced interface id, x/y offsets, two booleans controlling proportional placement, x/y float multipliers and two integer caps.

InterfaceLayoutManager resolves the referenced entry, optionally multiplies its width/height by the stored float factors, applies the integer offsets and enforces the stored width/height caps before positioning the dependent child.
InterfaceLayoutEntry constructs and owns this object only through its relative-layout configuration method.
